docker.cpu.system.ref: Datadog: integrations-core@a9b9e42 docker_daemon/metadata.csv docker.cpu.system: gauge, percent, no per-unit, 'percent of time ... of this container, unnormalized'. Check: datadog-agent@7.85.2 (c7e9b19) pkg/collector/corechecks/containers/generic/processor.go:177 submits container.cpu.system (cgroup system CPU time, ns) with sender.Rate; docker/adapter.go:19,54 renames it docker.cpu.system and divides by 1e7 (generic/adapters_utils.go:10 ConvertNanosecondsToHz), so 100 = one full core. OTel: collector-contrib@v0.165.0 receiver/dockerstatsreceiver/metadata.yaml container.cpu.usage.kernelmode: monotonic cumulative sum, ns. Units: percent vs ns; rate() gives ns/s; scale 1e-07 = the Agent's / 1e7. type deviation: metadata.csv says gauge, but the Agent submits a Rate of a cumulative counter (processor.go:177), stored in-app as gauge. vendor deviation: the table has no docker.* row; adapter.go:19 renames Datadog container.cpu.system to docker.cpu.system. The table maps container.cpu.system to container.cpu.usage.system, but the receiver documents that metric as 'the usage for the system, not the container'. The Agent value is the container's kernel-mode time (pkg/util/containers/metrics/docker/collector_linux.go:37 UsageInKernelmode; cgroup v2 cpu.stat system_usec), i.e. container.cpu.usage.kernelmode ('time spent by tasks of the cgroup in kernel mode'). Dash0: fixtures/oracle/dash0_default_metrics.yaml lists container.cpu.usage.kernelmode (sum); Dash0 live 2026-11-08, dataset default, read-only: count by (container_name, container_image_name) (last_over_time({otel_metric_name="container.cpu.usage.kernelmode"}[24h])) = 23 series. Labels: the Agent tagger (comp/core/tagger/collectors/workloadmeta_extract.go:233,244) sets container_name = container name and docker_image = <image>:<tag>; Dash0 container_name and container_image_name have the same form (e.g. postgres:18.6). Untagged images: the Agent appends :latest (comp/core/workloadmeta/def/types.go:337); all 23 Dash0 images are tagged. Dash0 also splits 20 container_id when enriched resource attributes change (e.g. os_description); avg then briefly counts both series.
